definition: As artificial intelligence (AI) has become more mainstream, there is growing concern about how this will influence elections.
details: Potential targets of AI include election processes, election offices, election officials and election vendors. There are also global efforts to improve elections using AI.

explainer.lead: AI can generate convincing text, images, audio and video, making it cheaper and easier to produce campaign material or misleading election content. Its use matters because the same technology can help campaigns reach voters and also deceive them or target election processes, offices, officials and vendors.

tiers.eli5: AI can work like a very convincing costume maker, creating a picture or voice that seems to belong to a real person. During an election, someone could use that costume to make a candidate appear to say something false, or a chatbot could give voters the wrong polling information. AI can also help, such as by translating speeches so more people understand them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers working on election integrity may encounter generated video, altered images, cloned speech and chatbot text across campaign and social-media systems. Practical work can include assessing public submissions of misleading media, as with India's open-source Deepfakes Analysis Unit, and checking chatbot claims about voting locations, times and methods. Rephrased prompts have been used to produce fraudulent emails and phishing websites, so prompt wording alone is not a reliable safeguard.
tiers.paperLevel: The topic covers AI-mediated effects on electoral processes, offices, officials, vendors and voters, including synthetic media, misinformation, persuasion, microtargeting, translation and candidate-information tools. In one comparison of policy messages, LLM-generated text scored 2.91 versus 2.80 for human text on smartness, and the generated messages tended to be more technical and analytical. Documented incidents do not establish a general estimate of electoral impact, and attribution can remain uncertain, as with the unknown party connection of Ghana's @TheTPatriots network.

explainer.example: During the 2023 Argentine primary elections, Javier Milei's team distributed AI-generated images, including a fabricated image of rival Sergio Massa that drew 3 million views. The team also created an unofficial Instagram account called "AI for the Homeland," while Massa's team distributed AI-generated images and videos as well.

usedIn.name: Political campaigns
usedIn.detail: Used for generated advertisements, campaign art, avatars, cloned candidate voices and targeted messages.

usedIn.name: Social media
usedIn.detail: Used to circulate deepfakes, fabricated images and partisan posts, sometimes through networks of fake accounts.

usedIn.name: Voter communication
usedIn.detail: Used for real-time speech translation and chatbots that explain a candidate's pledges.

usedIn.name: Content assessment
usedIn.detail: India's Deepfakes Analysis Unit provides an open-source platform for sharing misleading content and assessing whether it was AI-generated.

explainer.intuition: The same generative tools can support legitimate outreach or create deceptive material at scale. Compared with earlier manipulation techniques, they can require little technical skill and allow content to spread rapidly.
howItWorks: A campaign or other actor uses generative AI to create text, images, video or speech.
The material may be ordinary campaign content, or deceptive content such as a candidate deepfake or false voting instructions.
Social accounts, chatbots, virtual rallies and targeted messages distribute it to voters.
Voters may be persuaded, confused or simply reached in another language.
Researchers and public platforms can assess suspicious material, although responsibility and electoral effects may remain unclear.
explainer.whyItMatters: Misleading synthetic content can affect what voters believe about candidates and how, when or where to vote, while election institutions and vendors are also potential targets. At the same time, AI offers benefits such as real-time translation and accessible candidate information, making election use a question of both risk and improvement.
misconceptions: AI in elections is not limited to deepfakes; it also includes chatbots, campaign art, avatars, targeted messages and live translation.
AI-generated content is not automatically deceptive, since campaigns have also used it openly for advertisements and candidate information.
A viral AI-generated post does not by itself identify its sponsor or prove that it changed the election result.
